newsitem.title: GERMANY: Korea tension highlights need to talk - Albright.
newsitem.headline: Korea tension highlights need to talk - Albright.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright expressed Washington's concern on Monday about events on the Korean peninsula, saying they underlined the need for dialogue between the rival North and South.

Albright said the United States would work to ensure there was no rise in the tension that has followed the defection of a North Korean official and the weekend shooting of another defector in Seoul by suspected North Korean agents.

"Obviously, we are concerned about events on the Korean peninsula and they just underline the importance of trying to establish a dialogue between North and South Korea," Albright said after meeting her German counterpart Klaus Kinkel.
"The Korean peninsula has been and continues to be of importance to the United States and we want to make sure that there not be any further exacerbation," she said.
She said recent developments highlighted the need for four-power talks involving the U.S., China and the two Korean states in a bid to achieve dialogue between Seoul and Pyongyang.
